summary: Set 117 Session 1 put per-launch platform-state isolation on the shared launch seam, covered it with falsifiable tests, and re-measured the Layer 3 worker curve on DENICI. Part of the isolation had landed before the session in commit 5388c3d1, which explicitly deferred three things here; this session did those three. makeLaunchStateDirs() now lives in scripts/vscode-launch.js and is called by BOTH launch sites -- the Playwright harness and scripts/stage-walk.js, which the earlier inline fix had missed, so `npm run walk` had still been launching against the operator's real machine-wide VS Code profile (L-069-1). HOME/USERPROFILE are scoped alongside APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA so the fix is not Windows-only, since Linux and macOS reach VS Code's machine-wide state through HOME. 17 new tests pair every positive assertion with its planted look-alike (L-112-1); both falsifiers were executed, and the first one caught a weak assertion of my own that matched a type declaration rather than a call. The DENICI sweep (35 tests, real-host-baseline excluded) ran green at 1/4/8/12 workers: 548s / 231s / 206s / 189s. The finding that matters is the shape, not the endpoint -- marginal wall clock per added worker is 105.7s (1->4), 6.3s (4->8), 4.3s (8->12), because each doubling inflates every individual test's own duration (2.46x the total work at w=12 for 2.90x the wall clock). The knee is at 4. TWO THINGS ARE DELIBERATELY UNRESOLVED AND MUST NOT BE READ AS SETTLED. First, the session's central hypothesis -- that the earlier failures and poor speedup were shared state rather than CPU -- is NOT settled: the previously-failing 8-worker configuration failed on the operator's 14-core work machine, a different physical machine unreachable from this session, so isolation and host changed together and neither can be credited. Verification raised this twice and rejected the first fix on the correct ground that documenting a missing measurement does not perform it; the operator adjudicated on 2026-08-10 to close with it as an owed residual OWNED BY SESSION 2 as a precondition before any worker count is adopted. Second, vsix-first-run-walkthrough failed in 2 of 9 full-suite runs with two distinct failure modes, and its cause is recorded as UNRESOLVED rather than as flakiness -- one mode persisted under full isolation at w=8, which spec step 4 requires be recorded as an open product-race candidate. An earlier draft of the evidence asserted three causal exclusions the sample sizes do not support; all three are withdrawn in the text with the reason each fails. TWO PRE-EXISTING close_session GATE DEFECTS SURFACED AT CLOSE, both diagnosed here. (1) working_tree_clean blocked on checklist-posts.jsonl -- the file the checklist post writes immediately before close -- which contradicted check_checklist_posted's own remediation ('post the checklist and re-run close') and left the SAMPLE PROJECT, the new-user path, unable to close at all. Operator-authorized fix applied: the basename joins session-events.jsonl in _WORKING_TREE_IGNORE_PATTERNS, with a falsifier proving the exemption stays narrow. That repaired sampleProjectSmoke, which had been red on master. (2) The falsifier then caught a larger one: working_tree_clean never blocks on MODIFIED tracked files at all, because _run_git strips git's leading space and the parser slices a fixed offset into the path. Operator directed it to its own session; written up with mechanism, reproduction and suggested fix in s1-found-defect-working-tree-clean.md. It did not block this close -- S1's tree is genuinely clean. Close suites on the final tree: Layer 3 FULL 36 passed (10.9 min at shipping workers:1), pytest 3852 passed / 5 skipped (-n 8 per the operator's cap), mocha 1690 passing / 0 failing.

reason.specifics: Session 2 quarantines real-host-baseline, sets the worker count, and builds the loud-retry path -- all of which consume this session's sweep and its two unresolved records directly, so continuity of that context is worth more than any model change. The consequential variable for Session 2 is NOT the model but the MACHINE: it carries an owed precondition to re-run the final-isolation 8-worker configuration on the operator's 14-core work host, which this session could not reach. Running Session 2 from the office machine discharges that residual naturally and should be preferred; running it from DENICI is legitimate but then the residual carries forward to Session 3 and must be restated, not dropped. Session 2 must also decide explicitly how to handle vsix-first-run-walkthrough in its three-consecutive-green control, and must not discount it as unrelated flake -- its cause is open and may be the very schedule sensitivity that control exists to detect.
